_note: Held or parried (2026-11-13): he holds the ball when his handling reaches difficulty = (offset / reach + speed / catch_speed_ref) / 2: together, at their references (a ball at catch_speed_ref at the edge of his reach), the two causes demand perfect hands, as catch_speed_ref is defined (derived from the definition, ADR-052 note; at 77-85 each alone did, and no ball was held). Before they multiplied and every save was held. The save (ADR-051, family 'in goal'). No die (ADR-035). The keeper starts to dive after his reaction time, reaction = slow - (slow - fast) x reactivity, in ticks (10 ticks = 1 s). In the time left before the ball reaches the goal plane he dives, at dive_speed x (0.5 + 0.5 x explosive_force), at most dive_max x (0.5 + 0.5 x explosive_force). His reach is his standing reach (half his height) plus the dive, measured from the centre of his body (body_centre_cm above the ground) to the point where the ball crosses the plane. If the ball is within reach he stops it; he holds it if his hands (goalkeeping, the prototype of handling, OI-92) are at least the difficulty (offset / reach) x (ball speed / catch_speed_ref), otherwise he parries it: the ball comes back at parry_rebound_milli of its speed, pushed away from the centre of the goal. A ball he reaches only at the edge of his reach (offset beyond tip_share_milli of it) is tipped: his touch turns it but does not stop it, and it goes on past the post (a corner when it crosses the goal line); nearer, a parry pushes it back into play (2026-11-13). Standing reach (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE): his reach before any dive is standing_reach_share of his height from the centre of his body (his arm span is about his height, plus a step): it was half his height, a keeper with his arms down. The shooter judging a chance imagines a keeper of reference_keeper_height_cm.
_source: Order of magnitude from observation of real keepers: a reaction of about 0.2 s (fast) to 0.5 s (slow); a lateral dive of about 4-5 m/s, reaching some 2 m beyond the standing reach. Arbitrary, declared, to be calibrated at L3 against real save rates (about seven shots on target in ten are saved).
